title: Ambient operation comparisons for finite scalar extension
statement: Let l be prime. Coefficient fields are finite extensions of Q_l with specified Q_l-algebra embeddings. Use the actual completed coefficient sheaves and raw rationalizations of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Schemes supporting a constructible rational category are assumed noetherian, finite-dimensional, with l invertible; ambient operation comparisons are for arbitrary scheme morphisms g : X → Y in the actual ambient derived categories. For finite coefficient fields E → F and scheme morphisms, the residue-normalized coefficient structure square gives the ordinary scalar-pullback comparison. Its specified adjunction mate is an isomorphism for direct image. Scalar extension commutes with completion via the isomorphism fixed by its unit equation, preserves complete objects, and therefore gives the specified completed-pullback comparison. For a cartesian square, the two specified routes comparing the E and F completed exchanges are equal, and any functor applied to their components preserves that equality.

source.place: Order 1307; existing scalar-extension component, relocated without changing signatures or proofs.

proof.text: Apply each finite coefficient projection to the coefficient structure square. Postcomposition by coefficient inclusions commutes with inverse image on continuous sections; constant-sheaf comparison and joint monicity of the completion projections give the square. Use the ordinary tensor-pullback comparison, and take its specified adjunction mate for the push comparison. Finite-free direct-image coherence proves this mate invertible.

Scalar tensor of the source completion output is target-complete, and exact coefficient restriction sends target-complete objects to source-complete objects. Use the specified scalar adjunction to transport the source reflection Hom bijection. Extend the scalar image of the source unit along the target completion unit, and extend the target unit along the scalar image of the source unit. The two Hom injections show the arrows inverse. The target reflection Hom injection proves naturality and uniqueness with the exact displayed unit equation. The existing preservation-of-completeness and completed-pullback proofs then apply unchanged.

The coefficient-exchange mate theorem compares the ordinary exchanges using the specified pull cube and push mates. The reflected adjunction coefficient square and ringed pushforward/completion comparison identify their completed versions. This gives equality of the two exact routes already defined in the statement. Applying a functor preserves the component equality.

J3 implements the normalized comparison, naturality, inverse equations and uniqueness; two concrete completeness transport steps remain as named sublemmas.
